insights.claim: The operator uses a Helm-rendering controller pattern rather than imperative resource construction, embedding two upstream charts and tracking a managedGVKs list for orphan pruning.
insights.reasoning: The managedGVKs list (line 61-71) enumerates all resource types the charts can produce, including cert-manager Certificates and Gateway API HTTPRoutes. This pattern enables declarative lifecycle management but requires the GVK list to be updated whenever chart templates add new resource types, creating a coupling risk between chart evolution and operator code.

insights.claim: Platform dependencies (cert-manager, Gateway API, prometheus-operator) are conditionally registered via REST mapper CRD detection, allowing the operator to run on clusters without these optional components.
insights.reasoning: The conditional owns pattern (lines 554-565) checks isCRDInstalled for each optional resource type before registering a watch. This is an established controller-runtime pattern for graceful degradation but means that CRDs installed after operator startup are not detected until restart.

insights.claim: The metrics Service on port 8443 has no authentication middleware; access control relies on Kubernetes NetworkPolicy or namespace isolation.
insights.reasoning: The metricsserver.Options only sets BindAddress without FilterProvider or SecureServing authentication. The programmatically created metrics Service exposes this endpoint cluster-internally. Unlike operators that use kube-rbac-proxy, this operator relies on network-level access control for metrics endpoint security.
